summary: Round-1 transactional verification. Wrote IN-PROCESS suite backend/tests/test_iter25_txn_recovery.py (isolated DB gymboss_txn_tests on rs0, httpx ASGITransport, Razorpay monkeypatched, DB dropped at end). 20 tests, 19 pass. Covered: all 15 fault checkpoints (member.create x3, renew x3, payment.record, payment.edit, payment.reverse x2, ledger.after_opening_invoice, subscription.after_ledger/after_grant/after_payment_row). Each one rolled back fully with no partial writes, and receipt counters were rolled back too. Retrying the same request then succeeded exactly once with correct balances. apply_payment: 5 concurrent calls with the same payment_id gave 1 grant. 2 different payment_ids gave +60 days with no lost update. When audit/track were patched to raise, the grant stayed committed and a retry returned None. claim_event states new/busy/stale->new/failed->new/duplicate all correct. Webhook crash at after_grant returned 500 and marked the event failed; redelivery granted once; a third delivery was duplicate; a new event id for the same payment did not grant twice. Idempotency-Key: replay works on all 4 endpoints. A cross-scope key returns 422. Concurrent same-key gather gave exactly 1 record for member create, payment and renew, with all responses 200. 5 concurrent renewals without a key all succeeded one after another: distinct cycle_keys, expiry = sum of cycles, due consistent. Edit racing reversal, including forced interleaving via a slowed checkpoint in both orders: always consistent, with reversal amount = -(final amount), one reversal, and edit getting 409 while the reversal holds the original. 5 concurrent double reversals gave exactly 1x200 and 4x404, with one negative entry. 3x migrate_all + migrate_member running concurrently gave exactly one opening invoice per member and balances equal to the pre-migration due; 2 concurrent run_migrations calls left one record. Razorpay cancellation: confirmed -> deleted and op succeeded and kept. Cancel fails with GET active -> 409, nothing deleted, op failed; reconcile later confirmed it (cancellations_confirmed>=1, attempts=2). Cancel raises but GET cancelled -> deletion proceeds. 5 billable statuses were all attempted and one failing blocked deletion; the retry cancelled only the remaining one. autodebit cancel returns 503 when unconfirmed and keeps the local status as active. ONLY FAILURE: concurrent DELETE /api/payments/{id} with the SAME Idempotency-Key returns [200,404,404,404] instead of replaying 200 (data is correct: one reversal). Regression over HTTP (iter22, 23, 13, 12, 20; 80 tests): 79 pass. The 1 failure was a stale iter13 assertion that expected reversed payments to disappear from the list; I fixed the test. Frontend: demo login -> member drawer -> record payment, renew, and reverse all work, and POST /payments, POST /members/{id}/renew and DELETE /payments/{id} carry an Idempotency-Key header. Found a UI bug in the Transaction History list.

minor.issue: Same Idempotency-Key sent concurrently (double tap / client retry while the first request is in flight): the losers get 404 'already reversed' instead of the replayed 200. RCA: the duplicate txn hits a WriteConflict, with_transaction retries, re-reads p.status=='reversed' and raises HTTPException(404). That is not a DuplicateKeyError, so commit() never consults idem_lookup. Fix: in reverse_payment, catch HTTPException 404 from commit(), then call idem_lookup(org_id,key,scope); if found, return the replay response. Alternatively, inside txn check idem doc before raising 404.

Only HTTPException is caught. billing.razorpay_request does not wrap httpx transport errors (timeout/ConnectError), so a network failure propagates and delete-account / autodebit cancel return a 500 instead of 409/503. The op record stays 'pending' with attempts 0 and no last_error, though reconcile still retries pending ops. Catch Exception, or wrap httpx errors in razorpay_request.

After cancellation is confirmed, the per-collection delete_many loop is not transactional or resumable. A crash midway leaves a half-deleted tenant whose org doc still exists. Consider marking org 'deleting' first and making the purge idempotent and resumable.

Key replay ignores the request body: the same key with a different amount silently returns the first result. This is acceptable, but consider storing a body hash and returning 422 on mismatch, as Stripe does.

ui_bugs.issue: Reversed originals and reversal entries still show Edit and Reverse buttons, with no 'Reversed' badge or strike-through. The negative reversal entry is rendered in green as '₹-100'. Clicking these buttons yields 409/404 errors. The fix is to hide the actions when p.status==='reversed' or p.type==='reversal', show a badge, and use danger color plus the '-₹' format for negative amounts.

action_items: reverse_payment: when the txn raises 404, consult idem_lookup and return the replay 200 (concurrent same-key reversal)
MemberDrawer: hide Edit/Reverse for reversed payments and reversal rows, add a Reversed badge, and render negative amounts correctly
cancel_remote_subscription: also catch non-HTTPException transport errors so delete-account returns 409 and the op is marked failed
Optional: make the account purge resumable; optional body-hash check on Idempotency-Key
critical_code_review_comments: Edit vs reversal: the edit can commit while a reversal txn is paused after inserting the negative entry, because the original has not been touched yet. The reversal then write-conflicts and retries with the edited amount, so the outcome is consistent (edited-then-reversed). This is correct, but it relies on with_transaction retry.

rca of the issue: Same-key concurrent reversal: requests A and B both pass idem_lookup (none saved yet). A commits. B's txn gets a WriteConflict on the payment doc, so with_transaction retries, the re-read sees status 'reversed' and raises HTTPException 404. members.commit() only maps DuplicateKeyError to the idempotent replay, so B returns 404. Repro: asyncio.gather 4x DELETE /api/payments/{id} with the same Idempotency-Key gives [200,404,404,404].
